information.description:
These aren’t your run-of-the-mill squad leaders, as they’ve almost all had time under fire and came out on top. They’re battle proven, and were thus promoted (and kitted out) appropriately so. Most often seen at the helm of heavier units protecting important locations to Barghest’s operations, such as the old EBM/Petrochem stadium.

From Corgo's 77 Collection: Mooks by Corgopolis (Barghest).

description.value: Experts in combat who use their fighting prowess to dominate in the lawless time of the Red.

Cost: Double the original weapon’s Cost + 500eb ♦ Availability: Price Category is increased by one tier

BARGHEST are bullies, but they also employ expert gunsmiths that kit out their troops with the best streetbuilt iron around. Yet, producing new models is expensive, so usually they just tweak existing ones scrounged from around Dogtown. These modifications include depleted uranium ammo, more reliable parts, and a battery of accessories to ensure a lethal bite.

A Darkhound Variant Weapon becomes Standard Quality if not already so (Unless it is Excellent Quality, in which case it remains as such), gains up to 500eb worth of Attachments/Mods, and whenever it would ablate armor, it now ablates 1 additional SP. When buying Ammunition for a Darkhound Variant Weapon, its Cost is doubled and Price Category increased by one (e.g, Armor-Piercing is 200eb (Expensive)) and can only be used by the weapon it is purchased for. Melee Weapons cannot have Darkhound Variants.

NOTE: While the above text are the typical guidelines for Darkhound Variant Weapons, the following set of preexisting Darkhound Weapons may have extra modifications done to them that might tweak their functions and performance on a case-by-case basis.

Assault Rifle (w/ Carbine Barrel, Constant Recoil System [Machine Gun 3], & Foregrip). Holds 30 Rounds. Deals 4d6 damage in Single Shot. While wielded in two hands, this weapon is considered Excellent Quality [Foregrip]. Ablates 1 additional SP whenever it would ablate armor.

The name of this semi-auto rifle refers to the nine-tailed fox of myth. No, the Kyubi doesn't have nine barrels, but with the way it rains bullets on your enemies, you wouldn't know. Tsunami Defense Systems strives for quality craftsmanship and unparalleled optics in all of its weapons. The Kyubi is no exception. Its factory-issue laser sight offers for precise marksmanship right out of the box. And while some scoff at the plastic casing, Tsunami's engineers stand by the design. They aren't cutting corners to to save money – they're delivering one of the lightest, reliable, and powerful rifles on the market.

Cost: 1,500eb (Very Expensive)

Stealth operators need discrete, form-fitted protection. That’s why Gibson Battlegear sells this modular, carbon composite neural-synched ballistic mask to spec ops all over the world.

SP9 Head Armor with no Armor Penalty. Has built-in Anti-Smog Breathing Mask and Smart Ears. Its visor may be raised/lowered as an Action. While the visor is lowered, this armor is considered to have a built-in Zetatech Tank Commander Headset (Going Quiet, pg. 7), and Human Perception Checks against the user suffer a -2 penalty.

‘NIGHTSTALKER’ BALLISTIC MASK

Cost: 5,000eb (Luxury)

A rare ballistic mask with a titanium-plated visor and an absurdly sized optical suite. Mostly used by assassins, spies, and other psycho-killers even capable of affording it.

SP11 Head Armor with no Armor Penalty. Has built-in Anti-Smog Breathing Mask, Smart Ears, and Smart Glasses. The Smart Glasses have pre-installed Targeting Scope and TeleOptics, which do not consume any Option Slots and cannot be removed. Its visor may be raised or lowered as an Action. While the visor is lowered, this helmet is considered to have a built-in Zetatech Tank Commander Headset, its user gains access to cybereye options installed in the Smart Glasses, and Human Perception Checks against the user suffer a -4 penalty.

From Corgo's 77 Collection V3 by Corgopolis (Armor & Fashion > Armor Catalog).

Internal Body Cyberware.

Use an Action to load one dose of Street Drug into a subdermal storage pod. Optionally, one can configure a Biomonitor to automatically dose the user upon entering combat, suffering a critical injury, or reaching a predetermined Wound State threshold.

Primary Effect

Dose lasts 24 hours.

  • The user rolls 2d6 Humanity Loss which is returned if they pass the Secondary Effect save
  • The user ignores Seriously Wounded wound states for the duration

Secondary Effect (DV17)

When the dose wears off, the user rolls WILL + Resist Torture/Drugs + 1d10 against Secondary DV.

  • On Fail Humanity loss is not returned
  • Unless experiencing the primary effect, REF -2
Deals no damage. If hit roll DV15 Resist Torture/Drugs. On a fail take the Damaged Eye and Damaged Ear Critical injuries (see pg. 188) for 1 minute. No Crit damage dealt.
